10116-all-saints-day-and-other-sermons.creator: Unknown
10116-all-saints-day-and-other-sermons.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. nd before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands; and cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb. And all the angels stood round about the throne, and about the elders and the four beasts, and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God, saying, Amen:  Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever.

arxiv-2003-01974.title: Flow Computation in Temporal Interaction Networks
arxiv-2003-01974.creator: Chrysanthi Kosyfaki, Nikos Mamoulis, Evaggelia Pitoura, Panayiotis Tsaparas
arxiv-2003-01974.description: Abstract Temporal interaction networks capture the history of activities between entities along a timeline. At each interaction, some quantity of data (money, information, kbytes, etc.) flows from one vertex of the network to another. Flow-based analysis can reveal important information. For instance, financial intelligent units (FIUs) are interested in finding subgraphs in transactions networks with significant flow of money transfers.

arxiv-2102-04595.title: BFV quantization of the nonprojectable
arxiv-2102-04595.description: Abstract 1 Introduction The Hořava theory of quantum gravity [ 1 ] can be formulated in two different versions. One is the projectable case, defined by the condition of the lapse function is a function only of time. The other version, the nonprojectable theory, has a lapse function that depends in general in time and space.

arxiv-2306-17272.title: Recognizing 𝐖 𝟐 \mathbf{W_{2}} Graphs
arxiv-2306-17272.creator: Vadim E. Levit
arxiv-2306-17272.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Vadim E. Levit. A set S ⊆ V ⁡ ( G ) S\subseteq V(G) is independent if its elements are pairwise nonadjacent. A vertex v ∈ V ⁡ ( G ) v\in V(G) is shedding if for every independent set S ⊆ V ⁡ ( G ) ∖ N ⁡ [ v ] S\subseteq V(G)\setminus N[v] there exists u ∈ N ⁡ ( v ) u\in N(v) such that S ∪ { u } S\cup\{u\} is independent.

arxiv-2402-14595.title: Agile Requirement Change Management Model for Global Software Development
arxiv-2402-14595.creator: Neha Koulecar, Bachan Ghimire
arxiv-2402-14595.description: Abstract We propose a noble, comprehensive and robust agile requirements change management (ARCM) model that addresses the limitations of existing models and is tailored for agile software development in the global software development paradigm. To achieve this goal, we conducted an exhaustive literature review and an empirical study with RCM industry experts.

arxiv-2408-12766.title: Learning Robust Features for Scatter Removal and Reconstruction in Dynamic ICF X-Ray Tomography
arxiv-2408-12766.creator: Siddhant Gautam, 1,* Marc L. Klasky, 2 Balasubramanya T. Nadiga, 2 Trevor Wilcox, 3 Gary Salazar, 4 and Saiprasad Ravishankar 1,5
arxiv-2408-12766.description: Abstract Density reconstruction from X-ray projections is an important problem in radiography with key applications in scientific and industrial X-ray computed tomography (CT). Often, such projections are corrupted by unknown sources of noise and scatter, which, when not properly accounted for, can lead to significant errors in density reconstruction.

arxiv-2412-06685.title: Policy Agnostic RL: Offline RL and Online RL Fine-Tuning of Any Class and Backbone
arxiv-2412-06685.creator: Max Sobol Mark, Tian Gao, Georgia Gabriela Sampaio, Mohan Kumar Srirama, Archit Sharma, Chelsea Finn, Aviral Kumar
arxiv-2412-06685.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Max Sobol Mark, Tian Gao, Georgia Gabriela Sampaio, Mohan Kumar Srirama, Archit Sharma, Chelsea Finn, Aviral Kumar. Recent advances in learning decision-making policies can largely be attributed to training expressive policy models, largely via imitation learning. While imitation learning discards non-expert data, reinforcement learning (RL) can still learn from suboptimal data.

arxiv-2502-17793.title: Synthia : Novel Concept Design with Affordance Composition
arxiv-2502-17793.creator: Hyeonjeong Ha, Xiaomeng Jin, Jeonghwan Kim, Jiateng Liu, Zhenhailong Wang, Khanh Duy Nguyen, Ansel Blume, Nanyun Peng, Kai-Wei Chang, Heng Ji
arxiv-2502-17793.description: Abstract Text-to-image (T2I) models enable rapid concept design, making them widely used in AI-driven design. While recent studies focus on generating semantic and stylistic variations of given design concepts, functional coherence —the integration of multiple affordances into a single coherent concept—remains largely overlooked.

arxiv-2511-16040.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Bayesian Clustering
arxiv-2511-16040.creator: Garritt L. Page, Andrés F. Barrientos, David B. Dahl, David B. Dunson
arxiv-2511-16040.description: Abstract Bayesian clustering methods have the widely touted advantage of providing a probabilistic characterization of uncertainty in clustering through the posterior distribution. An amazing variety of priors and likelihoods have been proposed for clustering in a broad array of settings. There is also a rich literature on Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms for sampling from posterior clustering distributions.

pmc-11536018.title: Protocatechuic acid attenuates intestinal inflammation through TLR4/p38 and NF-κB pathways in heat-stressed broilers
pmc-11536018.creator: Shuaiyong Wang, Xin Wang, Yu Gao, Yuchen Fu, Zhaoqing Han, Ping Xu, Jianli Tang
pmc-11536018.description: Protocatechuic acid (PCA), a major active component found in Eucommia ulmoides Oliver, is involved in regulating oxidative stress and inflammation. Heat stress poses a significant threat to the poultry industry. In this study, we investigated the protective effect of PCA on intestinal homeostasis under heat stress. Our results indicated that PCA improved the growth performance of broilers during heat stress.

pmc-11677089.title: Does Combined Treatment with Tranexamic Acid and Vancomycin Affect Human Chondrocytes In Vitro?
pmc-11677089.creator: Mike Wagenbrenner, Tizian Heinz, Philip M Anderson, Ioannis Stratos, Joerg Arnholdt, Susanne Mayer-Wagner, Konstantin Horas, Denitsa Docheva, Boris M Holzapfel, Maximilian Rudert, Manuel Weißenberger, Qian Chen
pmc-11677089.description: Background: The aim of our study was to examine the combined effects of tranexamic acid (TXA) and vancomycin powder (VP) on chondrocytes in vitro. Despite the use of TXA and VP being linked to a reduced risk of extensive postoperative blood loss and periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs) in TKA, the possible cytotoxic side effects on periarticular cell types remain unclear.

pmc-11692668.title: UNDERSTANDING BARRIERS TO PARTICIPATE IN DEMENTIA RESEARCH AMONG OLDER ADULTS IN THE BRONX, NEW YORK
pmc-11692668.creator: Oshadi Jayakody, Mirnova Ceide, Morgan Grabanski, Claudene George
pmc-11692668.description: The Bronx County in New York (NY) has the highest prevalence of dementia in the state and is considered the least healthy of NY counties. This study aims to identify the barriers to participation in dementia research among older adults in the Bronx and explore strategies for improving their research readiness.

pmc-12374996.title: Steering strategies for wasp inspired self propelled needles
pmc-12374996.creator: Jette Bloemberg, David Justin Jager, Paul Breedveld, Aimée Sakes
pmc-12374996.description: Positioning a thin needle into a solid substrate near a target region is difficult because the needle can easily bend and buckle. Nevertheless, in nature, female parasitic wasps can do this by using buckling prevention and steering mechanisms. This study presents a self-propelled needle that incorporates wasp-inspired steering mechanisms, specifically, the use of pretension and asymmetry within the needle segments.

pmc-12419000.title: Tweaking the electrocatalytic efficiency of sonochemically synthesized Bi2S3 nanorods through decoration with f-MWCNTs: A selective on-site detection of METOL in environmental samples
pmc-12419000.creator: Harikrishnan Sathya, Amal A Abdel Hafez, Mani Govindasamy, Pin-Yi Chen
pmc-12419000.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Graphical abstractKeywords: Bismuth sulfide, Health care analysis, Good health and well-being, Sonochemical synthesis, Electrochemical sensor, Clean Water

Introduction

The ultrasonic synthsis of nanocomposites has emerged as a green and efficient approach. In recent years, significant attention has been directed towards the ultrasound-assisted synthesis of various nanoparticles and nano-composite materials, particularly those involving transition metal oxides, metal sulfides, and carbon nanomaterials due to their ability to enhance dispersion and reduce particle aggregation [1,2]. The sonochemical method uses ultrasound to trigger cavitation in solution.

pmc-12449294.title: Analytical fidelity calculations for photonic linear cluster state generation
pmc-12449294.creator: Rohit Prasad, Simon D. Reiß, Giora Peniakov, Yorick Reum, Peter van Loock, Sven Höfling, Tobias Huber-Loyola, Andreas Theo Pfenning
pmc-12449294.description: By precisely timed optical excitation of their spin, optical emitters such as semiconductor quantum dots or atoms can be harnessed as sources of linear photonic cluster states. This significantly reduces the required resource overhead to reach fault-tolerant optical quantum computing.

pmc-12471576.title: Optimization of Pulsed Laser Cladding for Reconditioning of Ni–Al–Bronze (NAB) Marine Propeller
pmc-12471576.creator: George Ciprian Iatan, Dan Cristian Cuculea, George Ardelean, Elena Manuela Stanciu, Alexandru Pascu
pmc-12471576.description: The materials used in the marine environment are generally selected for their high performances in aggressive operational media. This is also the case for marine propellers, which are mainly manufactured from cast nickel–aluminum bronze (NAB), due to their favorable mechanical properties and corrosion resistance.

pmc-12594066.title: Unpacking medication choices: Key factors influencing treatment decisions in children with newly diagnosed attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
pmc-12594066.creator: Nidhi Chauhan, Velprashanth Venkatesan, Akhilesh Sharma, Ruchita Shah, Sandeep Grover, Debashish Basu
pmc-12594066.description: Background:Following a diagnosis of Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) many children require immediate use of pharmacological agents for symptom control, while for some children a trial of non-pharmacological management may be warranted initially.Aim:To study and identify the clinical and socio-economic factors associated with immediate use of pharmacotherapy versus non pharmacological management in children with newly diagnosed ADHD.

pmc-12773522.title: Abstract 211: Comparing Early and Late Window 3mm Trevo Stent Retriever Performance in Medium Vessel Occlusion Thrombectomy
pmc-12773522.creator: Manisha Koneru, Christopher Zhao, James E Siegler, Nicholas Vigilante, Jane Khalife, Daniel Tonetti, Hamza Shaikh
pmc-12773522.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionEndovascular thrombectomy has been shown to be beneficial for select patients with medium vessel occlusion ischemic strokes. Newer mechanical thrombectomy devices have designs to facilitate navigation of the medium and distal cerebrovasculature.

pmc-12840190.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Expression Analysis of the SUC Gene Family in Peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) Reveals Its Role in Seed Sucrose Accumulation
pmc-12840190.creator: Zongqin Feng, Qinqin He, Yixiong Zheng, Yu Zhang, Xiaolin Chen, Jiping Liu, Xinmin Huang
pmc-12840190.description: Sucrose is a key quality trait in peanuts, yet high-sucrose varieties are scarce. Although sucrose transporters (SUT/SUC) play crucial roles in sucrose transport and accumulation during seed development, systematic analyses in peanuts are limited. This study conducted a genome-wide analysis of the SUC gene family in cultivated peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.).

pmc-13070826.title: Vitamin D status, supplementation, and multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13070826.creator: Yanyan Li, Ying Xu, Xiaorui Pei, Ziqi Liu, Dan Gao, Lili Ma, Yan Wang, Yanan Fang, Ying Cai
pmc-13070826.description: BackgroundMultiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic immune-mediated neurodegenerative disorder of the central nervous system and a leading cause of disability among young adults. The disease exhibits considerable heterogeneity in clinical progression, with some patients experiencing more aggressive disease activity and a rapid decline in quality of life.

pmc-13223521.title: Psychometric properties of the hematopoietic cell transplantation frailty scale: A prospective observational study
pmc-13223521.creator: Luz Alejandra Lorca, Barbara Puga Larrain, Ivana Gonzalez Valdivia, Javiera Molina, Ivana Leao Ribeiro
pmc-13223521.description: IntroductionFrailty is common in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, thereby increasing toxicity risk and reducing post-transplant survival. This study evaluated the psychometric properties of the Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation Frailty Scale to assess transplant candidates. Additionally, it characterized the participants` sociodemographic and clinical profiles.MethodsOne hundred and two patients with hematologic malignancies participated in the study.

pmc-13253416.title: Case Report: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis masquerading as drug-induced liver injury: successful treatment with low-dose ruxolitinib and glucocorticoids
pmc-13253416.creator: Yang Dai, Luocheng Zhang, Xushu Zhong, Ailin Zhao, Ting Niu
pmc-13253416.description: BackgroundHemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome that can present with drug-induced liver injury (DILI), often mimicking acute liver failure and delaying diagnosis. Therapeutic options are limited in patients with severe hepatic dysfunction.ObjectivesTo describe the clinical features, treatment, and outcomes of three adult patients presenting with DILI-mimicking HLH and evaluate the effectiveness of low-dose ruxolitinib combined with corticosteroids.

pmc-13256907.title: From Pathway Tracing to Actionable Targets: Integrative Mendelian Randomization and Experimental Triangulation Map Metabolic Pathways Across Ovarian Cancer Histotypes
pmc-13256907.creator: Xinqi Wang, Haoyu Wang, Siyuan Hu, Wenyi Zhang, Huiyu Chen, Ying Shen, Hongyang Xue, Li Hong
pmc-13256907.description: Ovarian cancer (OC) comprises multiple histotypes with distinct mechanisms, molecular features, and clinical behavior. We used Mendelian randomization (MR) to map histotype-stratified metabolic pathways and connect them to drug targets, establishing a translatable target–metabolic node–histotype risk chain. We built a multi-stage MR framework using Integrative Epidemiology Unit (IEU) OpenGWAS summary statistics.

pmc-13264447.title: Good things come in threes: evaluating clinical utility of machine learning-derived clusters
pmc-13264447.creator: Daniil Lisik, Jip W T M De Kok, Nicolás Bermúdez Barón, Lowie E G W Vanfleteren, Bright I Nwaru, Rani Basna

pmc-13460131.title: Draft genome sequence of Enterobacter roggenkampii strain MBBL_MP5 isolated from dairy cow with clinical mastitis
pmc-13460131.creator: Kh. Yeashir Arafat, Md. Morshedur Rahman, Md. Anamul Kabir Hemal, Sourav Karmakar, Md. Samiul Islam Shanto, Tofazzal Islam, M. Nazmul Hoque
pmc-13460131.description: We report the draft genome of Enterobacter roggenkampii MBBL_MP5 isolated from milk of a dairy cow with clinical mastitis. The ~4.7 Mbp genome of MBBL_MP5 encodes 21 antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and 87 virulence factor genes (VFGs), highlighting its possible role in bovine mastitis and relevance to public health.

pmc-13461147.title: Divergent C. elegans toxin alleles are suppressed by distinct mechanisms
pmc-13461147.creator: Stefan Zdraljevic, Laura Walter-McNeill, Giancarlo N Bruni, Joshua S Bloom, JB Collins, Daniel HW Leighton, Heriberto Marquez, Noah Alexander, Leonid Kruglyak, Vincent J Lynch, Stefan Zdraljevic, Laura Walter-McNeill, Giancarlo N Bruni, Joshua S Bloom, Daniel HW Leighton, Heriberto Marquez, Noah Ale
pmc-13461147.description: Toxin-antidote elements (TAs) are selfish DNA sequences that bias their transmission to the next generation. TAs typically consist of two linked genes: a toxin and an antidote. The toxin kills progeny that do not inherit the TA, while the antidote counteracts the toxin in progeny that inherit the TA.

pmc-13499104.title: Pediatric intraorbital wooden foreign body mimicking an orbital mass: Delayed diagnosis and imaging considerations on MRI
pmc-13499104.creator: Henok Ayene, Bethelhem Belachew, Alemayehu Bedane Worke, Eyasu Altamo, Asrat Sime, Teferi Girma
pmc-13499104.description: Wooden intraorbital foreign bodies (IOFBs) are uncommon in children and may present a significant diagnostic challenge because their imaging appearance can mimic orbital neoplasms or inflammatory lesions, particularly when the trauma history is absent or unrecognized. We report the case of a 10-year-old boy presenting with progressive left orbital swelling and pain.

pmc-13515132.title: Ocular Syphilis in the Era of Resurgence: Clinical Characteristics and Diagnostic Challenges in a Single-Center Cohort
pmc-13515132.creator: Şerife Altun Demircan, Gülşah Gelişigüzel, Gozde Orman, Esra Kaya Kılıç, Salih Cesur, Günay Tuncer Ertem, Sengül Üçer, Çiğdem Ataman Hatipoğlu, Sami Kınıklı

pmc-13521922.title: Dynamic remodeling of the pancreas immune landscape in obesity
pmc-13521922.creator: Alexey Koshkin, Kranthi Kiran Kishore Tanagala, Anna Eichinger, Michael Chait, Aoife Young, Shanila Shakil, Junichi Yoshikawa, Yosuke Sakamoto, Steven B. Wells, Ladan Fazlollahi, Xiaojuan Chen, Boris Reizis, Donna L. Farber, Stuart P. Weisberg

pmc-13592195.title: Decoding clinical heterogeneity and age-related coronary risk in incomplete Kawasaki disease: a multicenter cluster analysis and structural equation modeling study
pmc-13592195.creator: Chang Liu, Dong Liu, Bin Li, Yanxia Xu, Zhongyou Tan, Ouyang Chen, Yanfeng Yang, Feifei Si, Wenliang Jiang, Qijian Yi, Fengchuan Jing
pmc-13592195.description: ObjectivesTo identify pretreatment clinical subphenotypes in incomplete Kawasaki disease (iKD) and examine their associations with post-IVIG coronary outcomes.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 1,619 iKD patients from six centers. Hierarchical clustering was performed using 11 pretreatment clinical and laboratory variables, with coronary measures excluded from cluster derivation. Post-IVIG coronary outcomes were subsequently compared across clusters.
